title: Prevent project-local validation build artifacts from entering SDK globs
description:
Problem: custom validation builds that set relative BaseOutputPath/BaseIntermediateOutputPath can create generated artifacts under each SDK project, for example MemorySmith.Core/artifacts/validation/obj/*.cs. SDK default item globs may then compile those generated files as source and produce duplicate assembly attribute errors. App/Core now exclude nested artifacts/**, but Storage/Tests do not and there is no shared repository-level guardrail.

Desired outcome: validation and workaround commands can use isolated outputs without polluting project directories or breaking later builds.

Scope:
- In scope: document safe custom build-output practices, move or duplicate MSBuild DefaultItemExcludes consistently across SDK projects, and add a hygiene check that flags generated artifacts/validation trees under project roots.
- Out of scope: changing normal bin/obj output behavior or deleting root-level artifacts used for reports.

Acceptance criteria:
- Repository guidance tells agents to use temp-directory absolute output paths for ad hoc isolated builds.
- A local validation or hygiene check reports project-local artifacts/validation directories under SDK projects.
- MSBuild exclusion is consistent across App/Core/Storage/Tests, preferably through a shared Directory.Build.props or equivalent, and excludes project-local artifacts from Compile/Content globs without hiding legitimate source files.
- The fix is validated by recreating an isolated-output scenario and confirming no duplicate compile inputs remain.

Validation:
- Run dotnet build MemorySmith.Core/MemorySmith.Core.csproj --nologo after cleanup.
- Run the new hygiene check if implemented.
- Run ./Scripts/Test-TaskRecords.ps1 after task metadata changes.

comments.author: AgentSmith
comments.body: Created during 2026-05-25 deepdive audit after an isolated-output test command created project-local artifacts/validation trees. Evidence: MemorySmith.Core/artifacts/validation/obj contained generated .cs files and a build previously failed with duplicate TargetFramework/AssemblyInfo attributes; cleanup removed MemorySmith.Core/App/Storage/Tests artifacts/validation and dotnet build MemorySmith.Core/MemorySmith.Core.csproj --nologo then passed. Renumbered from initial TSK-0153 because a user-created health-page task already owned that key.

comments.author: AgentSmith
comments.body: Scope refined after verification: MemorySmith.App.csproj and MemorySmith.Core.csproj already set DefaultItemExcludes for nested artifacts/**, but MemorySmith.Storage.csproj and MemorySmith.Tests.csproj do not. Remaining value is consistency, centralization, and a validator/hygiene check rather than treating App/Core as wholly uncovered.
